With respect to cost allocation, FERC Order 1920 requires: • Development and tariff inclusion of one or more default (ex ante) cost allocation methods for new long-term regional transmission facilities • Flexibility to allow for a state agreement approach process for voluntary cost allocation methods associated with specific long-term regional transmission facilities • Engagement with relevant state entities on cost allocation methods. The discretion granted to transmission providers to develop their own cost allocation methods in compliance with FERC regulations allows regions to innovate and develop cost allocation approaches that reflect regional preferences and system conditions. However, competing interests from different network users have also led to disputes. Further, transmission providers, FERC, and courts do not always agree on the appropriate cost allocation method or conclusions of the implementing entity.
